title: Introduce regional soft-quarantine and backpressure smoothing to stop spillover fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-03-06 revealed that an aggressive region-decommission pathway combined with noisy node health signals caused an immediate, hard drain of a primary region. That hard drain triggered large volumes of traffic to be re-routed to secondary regions and lower-cost model variants. The surge exceeded those variants' capacity and activated cascading fallback logic, resulting in increased tail latency, elevated cost, and ~12% of active customer sessions experiencing degraded responses for ~42 minutes. This ticket captures the incident analysis, short-term mitigations, and a proposal for a permanent fix centered on two new mechanisms: regional soft-quarantine (a graded drain state) and backpressure smoothing (signal damping + swap rate limiting).
timeline: 2026-03-06 02:11 UTC: Automated healthchecks in us-west reported 40% node degradation; control plane computed immediate drain weights
2026-03-06 02:12 UTC: Routing service applied hard drain (weight -> 0) within 30s due to low TTL and lack of consensus check
2026-03-06 02:13 UTC: Traffic shifted to fallback regions and variant-swap logic started replacing high-capacity variants with lower-cost quantized variants
2026-03-06 02:16 UTC: Secondary variant pools reached saturation; automated fallback escalations triggered additional swaps and increased cross-region egress
2026-03-06 02:36 UTC: Pager alerted; on-call triaged and applied manual partial-weight rollback to smooth routing over 10 minutes
2026-03-06 02:53 UTC: System stabilized; manual mitigation reverted hard-drain and restored normal variant distribution
root_cause: Three factors compounded: (1) healthchecks produced transient degradation spikes due to a noisy KV cache update causing short-lived CPU soft-faults; (2) control-plane drain logic treats drain as binary and lacks a consensus/validator step for cross-region confirmation; (3) variant-swap policy had no circuit-breaker on swap-per-minute, allowing rapid, multiplicative fallbacks under sudden load shifts.
mitigations_taken: Rolled back hard drains to partial weights to re-balance traffic
Raised emergency throttle on variant-swap pipeline to limit swaps to one per 60s per route
Enabled temporary routing weight smoothing (10s exponential decay) across the fleet
permanent_fixes_proposed: Regional soft-quarantine: introduce a graded drain state (active -> soft-quarantine -> hard-drain) with configurable dwell times and cross-region consensus check
Backpressure smoothing: implement exponential moving average on drain signals and on routing weight deltas to prevent step changes
Variant-swap circuit-breaker: limit swap rate and add global swap budget per customer tier to avoid multiplicative fallbacks
Consensus drain validator: require 2 independent control-plane signals (health ticks + telemetry anomaly) before promoting a region to hard-drain
Weight-bleed damping: cap per-minute routing weight change per region and per tier; queue excess adjustments to a graded rollback window
implementation_notes: Design doc created and attached (drive link). Implementation is split across control-plane and routing agent: control-plane will manage state transitions and consensus validator; edge routing agent will honor soft-quarantine states and apply EMA smoothing locally. Variant-swap circuit-breaker will be implemented in the swap orchestrator with a leaky-bucket rate limiter and a global dashboard for budgets.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): deploy soft-quarantine and smoothing to staging + 2 dev regions for 48h with synthetic chaos (node flaps) monitoring. Phase B: enable in a small subset of customers (5% traffic) for 72h. Phase C: global rollout with telemetry thresholds and automatic rollback. Feature flags will gate all changes; default behavior remains unchanged until Phase C completion.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: regional draining heatmap and variant-swap alarm panel
Alerts: page when swap_rate_per_route > 5 swaps/min sustained for 3m or when regional weight_change_rate_per_minute > 25%
postmortem_notes: Lessons learned: runbook assumed drains would be rare and binary — that assumption breaks under noisy signals. Future protective controls should be layered: signal smoothing, consensus checks, and swap rate-limits together prevent emergent cascades. The team determined rolling back hard-drain previously was the fastest mitigation; automating a graceful partial-weight fallback could remove the need for manual intervention.
